title: Leaf-photo plant disease check for home gardeners
one_liner: Let a gardener photograph a sick leaf with their phone and get told which disease it probably is.
problem: Home gardeners cannot tell plant diseases apart, so they either do nothing or spray the wrong treatment.
description: A phone app where the gardener photographs a leaf that looks wrong. An image classifier trained on labelled photographs of diseased leaves returns the three most likely diseases with a confidence for each, plus a short description of what to do about the top one. The claim is that most common garden diseases are visually distinctive enough that a phone photo is sufficient, so no lab test or expert is needed for the everyday cases.

sections.technique: Fine-tune an off-the-shelf image classifier on a public dataset of labelled diseased-leaf photographs. The app sends the photo to a server, the server returns the top three labels with confidences. Show the top three, not just the best guess, so the gardener can tell when the model is unsure.
open_questions: Do photos taken in a real garden work as well as the clean dataset photos taken against a plain background?
How should the app behave when the model is unsure about all three guesses?
